statements.t: “With strong performance across nearly every part of the core imaging center business, we are again raising certain guidance ranges in anticipation that full-year results will exceed both our original expectations and the revised ranges issued in conjunction with first and second quarter 2026 results.
We are raising 2026 Imaging Center guidance ranges for Revenue, Adjusted EBITDA (1) and Free Cash Flow (2) ,” added Dr.
Berger continued, “We are particularly excited about the opportunities for growth and expansion that will be made possible as a result of the recently announced pending acquisition of ONRAD.

The strategic fit that ONRAD’s capabilities have with both RadNet’s core imaging center business and Digital Health solutions is already being recognized in the imaging marketplace, and we look forward to the opportunities that could result once the acquisition is closed.”
As a result, we are raising its guidance ranges for Revenue, Adjusted EBITDA (1) and Free Cash Flow (2) .
In the Digital Health segment, we are raising the Adjusted EBITDA (1) guidance range as a result of effective expense management and faster-than-projected integration of acquired operations.”

statements.t: • anticipated trends in our revenues, operating expenses or capital expenditures, and our financial guidance;
• expected timing and potential impact of regulatory changes affecting our business;
• expected future market acceptance for our products or services, and our competitive strengths in the markets we serve;
• our ability to successfully acquire and integrate new businesses, and achieve expected benefits, synergies or operating results from those acquisitions; and
• economics and cost savings anticipated to be derived from our investments in artificial intelligence and machine learning products and solutions.

Our centers provide physicians with imaging capabilities to facilitate the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and disorders and may reduce unnecessary invasive procedures, often reducing the cost and amount of care for patients.

Gleamer products have already been deployed at RadNet imaging centers in California, Arizona, Maryland, New York and Florida, and we expect them to be rolled out across most RadNet centers by the end of 2026.

We have largely realized the anticipated cost synergies from these acquisitions and expect to benefit from cross-selling and upselling opportunities beginning in 2027 as we market our offerings as an integrated portfolio on the DeepHealth Radiology AI Suite.

Key developments during the quarter included the continued expansion of Reporting Pro, our proprietary diagnostic reporting solution, to sites in Arizona, California, Indiana and the Northeast, and we expect to complete deployment across our network by the first quarter of 2027.
Our service fee revenue is based upon our management's estimate of amounts we expect to be entitled to receive from patients and third-party payors.

We also record estimated implicit price concessions (based primarily on historical collection experience) related to uninsured accounts to record self-pay revenue at the estimated amounts we expect to collect.
We expect the segment to continue operating at a net loss in the near term as we continue integrating iCAD, See-Mode, CIMAR and Gleamer and investing in the segment’s growth.

As noncontrolling interests only represent a portion of our imaging center business, and excludes our Digital Health segment, which generated operating losses of $22.4 million and $54.8 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, we do not expect changes in net income attributable to noncontrolling interests to correlate with changes in consolidated operating income or pretax income.

We expect our existing capital resources, anticipated cash from operations and our borrowing capacity under our credit facilities will be sufficient to sustain our operations for the next twelve months and the foreseeable future.

We expect to fund any future acquisitions primarily with cash flow from operations and borrowings, including borrowing available under our secured credit facilities or through new equity or debt issuances.
We expect to fund the cash portion of the acquisition through existing cash balances and available borrowing capacity under our credit facilities.

estimates.name: Use of Estimates
estimates.t: The financial statements included in this report were prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), which requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes.

estimates.name: Revenues
estimates.t: Management continually reviews the contractual estimation process to consider and incorporate updates to laws and regulations, changes in business and economic conditions, and the frequent changes in managed care contractual terms resulting from contract re-negotiations and renewals.

estimates.name: Accounts Receivable
estimates.t: Our estimates and assumptions for allowances on our account receivable did not change materially during the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

estimates.name: Business Combination
estimates.t: Once a purchase has been determined to be the acquisition of a business, we are required to recognize the assets acquired and the liabilities assumed at their acquisition date fair values.
